extracted.intended_audience: aspiring fiction writers (especially young writers); readers moving toward writing
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and instructional standards for writing fiction, drawn from John Gardner's The Art of Fiction; covers theoretical (aesthetics, what fiction is) and practical/technical aspects (plot, sentence shape, diction, point of view).

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles and techniques of good writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Explains, simply and cogently, the principles and techniques of good writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Based on Gardner's courses and seminars; the book is a practical, instructive handbook that exemplifies lessons with detailed excerpts from classic works of literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensiveness of topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Sweeps across a complete range of topics — from the nature of aesthetics to the shape of a refined sentence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The book covers both broad theoretical concerns and fine-grained technical matters, implying a standard that useful craft guidance should be wide-ranging and cover multiple levels of craft.

rubrics_metrics.name: The nature of aesthetics
rubrics_metrics.description: Explores the nature of aesthetics as it pertains to fiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as part of the foundational, first-half inquiry into 'what fiction is', suggesting attention to aesthetic principles that underlie good fiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shape of a refined sentence
rubrics_metrics.description: Attention to the 'shape of a refined sentence' — the form and craft of sentence-level writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes sentence-level refinement as a distinct area of craft; paired elsewhere with 'sentence structure' and use of examples to show good vs. bad sentences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigation of 'what fiction is'
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigates, conceptually, 'just what fiction is' (theoretical understanding of fiction's nature).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gardner devotes the first half of the book to this inquiry, indicating a criterion that writers should understand fiction's aims and modes, not only technical methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of specific technical matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Addresses specific technical matters of fiction-writing in a focused way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gardner devotes the second half of the book to these matters, implying craft guidance should move from theory to concrete technique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plot
rubrics_metrics.description: Understanding and mastery of plot: 'the mysteries of plot' are a central technical area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gardner 'unravels the mysteries of plot' using examples across the canon (Homer to Kafka to Joyce Carol Oates), indicating use of canonical exemplars to teach plotting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentence structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Mastery of sentence structure as a technical criterion for good fiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discussed alongside 'shape of a refined sentence' and shown with 'good and bad examples', highlighting formal sentence construction and its effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diction
rubrics_metrics.description: Appropriate and effective word choice (diction) as a standard of craft.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed among core technical areas (plot, sentence structure, diction, point of view) that Gardner 'unravels' through examples and judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Point of view
rubrics_metrics.description: Use and control of point of view as a fundamental craft dimension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly named as one of the 'mysteries' treated with examples; implies attention to narrator choice, perspective, and consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of examples and judgments (good vs. bad examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Teaching by detailed excerpts and by showing 'good and bad examples and judgments.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gardner exemplifies lessons with detailed excerpts from classic works and issues judgments (positive and negative), implying that clear exemplars and critique are essential instructional tools for evaluating fiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pedagogical voice: critic, mentor, encourager
rubrics_metrics.description: A tone that combines critique and encouragement — serving as 'critic, mentor, and friend' to the writer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Praised as 'a necessary handbook, a stern judge, an encouraging friend' for young writers; implies evaluative feedback should be both honest and supportive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Canonical breadth of illustrative examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Draws examples from a wide literary range (e.g., 'from Homer to Kafka to Joyce Carol Oates').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using a wide sweep of canonical and varied examples is presented as a mark of thorough instruction and as a method for illustrating craft principles across contexts.
